column3: The absence of questioning between intimate companions concerns human relations, not divine accountability.
It limits blame after a proportionate response to wrongdoing, offering only a broad accountability parallel.
The question to Ibrahim identifies an agent for a deed, a limited human-scale counterpart to being answerable for action.
It distinguishes each side's responsibility for its own acts, though it does not state the Creator-creature asymmetry.
God's creation not being play supports the purposeful divine order in which the focus distinguishes Creator and creatures.
Recording everything people did supplies documentary grounds for creaturely accountability.
The honored servants neither precede God in speech nor act except by His command, sharply displaying their subordinate agency.
All beings belong to God and even those near Him serve without pride, establishing the creaturely status behind their answerability.
Pharaoh's accusation about Musa's past deed is a remote instance of a human being called to account.

The challenge whether earthly gods can raise the dead directly tests and denies their supposed divine agency.
Lut's conditional appeal to his daughters does not materially illuminate the focus.
God alone creates, provides, causes death, and gives life; the question whether partners can do any of this directly grounds His unique agency.

Sudden arrival while unaware does not clarify the accountability asymmetry.

Musa acknowledges a past act while qualifying his former state, a limited instance of personal responsibility.
The inhabitants of Hell not hearing there adds no material connection.

Asking for news from outside the battle is not the kind of questioning at issue.
Those who wronged themselves deny evil deeds, but God knows what they did, directly establishing accountable action before divine knowledge.
The question to prior messengers tests the legitimacy of worshipping any gods besides the Merciful.
Those who commit grave violations meet sin, connecting creaturely action to its inescapable consequence.
God's encompassing knowledge, permitted intercession, and the angels' fear together display the dependence of all creatures before Him.
The fulfilled promise confirms divine reliability, but does not specifically explain the focus's question-and-answer relation.
Specific communal violations receive disgrace and severe punishment, while God is not unaware of what they do.
God's recompense of the pious is a broad judgment parallel without the focus's distinct asymmetry.
Questioning among those in Paradise is social recollection rather than judicial accountability.
Their resolve to exclude the poor does not clarify the focus's divine authority relation.

Mutual questioning in Paradise does not bear on creatures answering to God.
Their failure to forbid wrongdoing they did directly identifies blameworthy collective action.
The gathered are explicitly stopped because they are to be questioned, directly supplying the human side of the focus.
Joseph recalls what his brothers did, a human confrontation with past conduct rather than final accountability.

God's stabilizing and guiding arrangement of the earth continues the surrounding demonstration of purposeful sovereign governance.
The demand to identify who acted against the idols exposes their need for human defenders and their lack of divine power.
The persecutors witness what they do to believers, making their own conduct evidence against them.
Their acknowledgment that the earth belongs to God advances the surrounding argument for His exclusive lordship.
A fulfilled divine promise of punishment is a broad example of effective divine action.
The warning not to obey a contemptible habitual swearer is unrelated to the focus.
God's protected sky is a sign from which people turn away, pairing His governance with their responsible refusal.

Neglect of prayer does not specifically clarify the focus's accountability asymmetry.
The question of who owns the earth and its inhabitants presses the hearers to acknowledge God's sole dominion.
Appeal to ancestral practice explains imitation but provides only a distant responsibility parallel.
The untroubled permanence of Paradise is not relevant to the focus.
God's creation and ordering of night, day, sun, and moon reinforces the sovereign agency argued throughout this passage.
The inevitable fulfillment of God's promise is only a general statement of effective divine action.

Restoring justice between fighting believers is a limited human analogue to judging wrongdoing.

The followers' accusation against their leaders is mutual blame among creatures rather than answerability before God.
The rebuke for saying what one does not do makes human speech answerable to actual conduct.
God's knowledge and non-rejection of good deeds offers a general accountability background.
The contrast between delivered truth and human lying frames false human claims as exposed before divine truth.
People must act to defend their idols, exposing the alleged gods' dependence and lack of independent agency.
Committing transgression and injustice leads to the Fire, a direct statement of creaturely action followed by divine judgment.
Dismissing the promise as ancient tales is a false human response but does not develop the focus's mechanism.
Creaturely worship and doing good are directed toward flourishing under the Lord's authority.
The plan to exclude a poor person does not clarify divine action or final questioning.
Those who fabricate lies about God are challenged to consider the Day of Resurrection, linking false claims to judgment.
The buried infant being questioned creates a stark judgment inquiry that exposes the accountability of those responsible.
Prior people's questioning and subsequent disbelief does not clarify the focus's Creator-creature distinction.
A people's difficulty understanding speech is unrelated to the focus.
The Fire tearing away the scalp has no material connection to questioning or agency.
The command to worship God alone supports monotheism generally, but not the specific accountability asymmetry.
Their answer that God created the heavens and earth supplies an acknowledged basis for His unmatched creative authority.
The ordering of prophetic and kinship relations does not illuminate the focus.
The fasting and marital regulations do not materially clarify divine unanswerability or creaturely questioning.
God brings people to account for what they conceal or disclose, directly establishing His comprehensive jurisdiction over creaturely acts.
Every soul finds its good and evil deeds present, supplying the realized-deed basis for accountability.
God's denial of injustice to servants qualifies His judgment as just rather than arbitrary.
God does not wrong even by an atom's weight, directly characterizing the justice of His judgment over creatures.
Messengers remove humanity's argument against God, reinforcing His unique judicial position.
God could have made one community but tests people through what He gave them, framing creaturely response under divine purpose.
God is the true Protector and swiftest in taking account, directly naming His exclusive accounting authority.
Angels demand that wrongdoers yield themselves and announce requital for false claims about God.
God gathers jinn and humans and questions the jinn about their human followers, directly staging creaturely accountability.
God asks jinn and humans whether messengers came and warned them of their meeting with Him.
Good and evil deeds receive their due multiple or equal recompense, with no injustice in the judgment.
God will question both the communities who received messengers and the messengers themselves.
The descendants are made to testify about God's lordship so they cannot deny it on the Day of Resurrection.
God will inform believers about the hypocrites and their deeds will be seen before they return to the Knower of the unseen.
God, His Messenger, and the believers will see what people do before they return to the Knower who informs them of their deeds.
Every soul learns what it sent ahead and is returned to God, its true Master.
No deed is absent from God's witnessing knowledge, grounding subsequent accountability.
God will judge disputed matters on the Day of Resurrection.
Witnesses testify against those who lied about God, placing false claims under divine judgment.
God repays everyone in full for what they did and is fully aware of their deeds.
Judgment belongs only to God, who commands exclusive worship.
Those who reject their Lord face the evil reckoning, making their response to Him accountable.
The faithful fear their Lord and the evil reckoning, directly identifying an answerable creaturely posture.
Whether judgment is shown in life or deferred, the reckoning belongs to God alone.
Abraham asks forgiveness for believers on the Day the account is established.
Every soul is repaid for what it earned, and God is swift in account.
Wrongdoers bear their own burdens and burdens from those they misled, connecting agency to answerable consequence.
God guides or lets stray whom He wills, and people will be questioned about what they did.
Each soul comes pleading for itself and is fully repaid for what it did without injustice.
Each person's record is fastened to them and produced as an open book on the Day of Resurrection.
The person is commanded to read their own record, being sufficient as their own reckoner that day.
No bearer bears another's burden, preserving individual responsibility before God.
Hearing, sight, and heart will each be questioned, specifying creaturely faculties as answerable.
Every people are called with their record or leader, and those given their book read it without the least wrong.
God alone knows the unseen and shares His judgment with no one, directly supporting His incomparable authority.
The book leaves no deed uncounted, and people find what they did present while God wrongs no one.
Everyone in the heavens and earth comes to the Most Merciful only as a servant.
Each creature comes to God individually on the Day of Resurrection.
The Hour is coming so that every soul may be repaid for what it strives for.
Whoever does righteous deeds while believing fears neither injustice nor deprivation in God's judgment.
God sets exact scales for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul is wronged and even a mustard seed is brought forth.
God does whatever He wills, after identifying all creation as subject to Him.
All sovereignty belongs to God on that Day, and He judges between people.
God's truthful record speaks against people and they are not wronged.
The denial that creation is purposeless culminates in humanity's return to God.
Whoever invokes another god without proof has their account with their Lord.
God knows people's present state and will inform them of what they did when they return to Him.
God knows what human hearts conceal and what they disclose, grounding accountable response.
God judges between people by His judgment and is the Mighty, Knowing.
God alone is worshipped, and all judgment and final return belong to Him.
All things perish except God; judgment belongs to Him and all return to Him.
The profession of faith is tested rather than left without examination.
God will inform people of what they used to do, following the command to resist obedience in associating partners with Him.
God judges between people on the Day of Resurrection concerning their disagreements.
Turning away after being reminded of God's signs is named as grave wrongdoing.
God recompenses the truthful for their truthfulness and punishes or accepts repentance from hypocrites.
God's knowledge distinguishes those who believe in the Hereafter from those who doubt it.
God gathers people and judges between them in truth as the Knowing Opener.
No soul bears another's burden, and God fully sees His servants.
God records what people send ahead and their traces, preserving every thing in a clear register.
All creatures will be brought before God, establishing universal summons to judgment.
No soul is wronged at all and is repaid only for what it used to do.
God does not approve disbelief for His servants but approves gratitude, tying creaturely response to His judgment.
God is the Originator and Knower of the unseen who judges between servants in their disputes.
The record is laid open, witnesses are brought, and people are judged in truth without injustice.
Every soul is paid in full for what it did, and God knows best what they do.
Every soul is repaid for what it earned on a day when there is no injustice and God is swift in account.
God judges in truth, while alleged partners cannot judge anything.
Human skin testifies against its owners and God makes all things speak, making creaturely acts answerable.
God does not wrong servants, even as each person bears the consequence of good or evil action.
God is the common Lord while each side bears its own deeds, excluding transfer of responsibility.
The challenge to partners who legislate without God's permission tests their claimed authority.
God declares that He did not wrong the punished; they were the wrongdoers.
God created the heavens and earth in truth so every soul may be repaid for what it earned without injustice.
Every community is called to its record on the Day of Judgment.
God's record speaks truthfully because He had people record what they did.
Each person has ranks according to what they did, and God repays them fully without injustice.
God knows the inner self more closely than a person's jugular vein, supporting complete accountability.
The two recording angels receive every utterance, furnishing evidence for judgment.
Every soul comes with a driver and a witness, a direct scene of compelled individual appearance.
God's word is not changed and He is not unjust to servants, defining the final judgment's authority and justice.
What is in the heavens and earth belongs to God so He may requite evil and reward good according to deeds.
No bearer bears another's burden, preserving personal answerability.
A person has only what they strive for, directly connecting agency and outcome.
God raises everyone and informs them of what they did, even deeds they forgot but God counted.
Each soul must consider what it has sent ahead for tomorrow, while God is aware of what people do.
Those who deny resurrection will be raised and informed of what they did; this is easy for God.
Disbelievers are told not to offer excuses because they are only being repaid for what they did.
God knows what hearts conceal, providing the interior scope of creaturely accountability.
On the Day of presentation, no secret of a person remains hidden.
Every soul is held in pledge for what it earned.
A person is informed on that Day of what they sent ahead and left behind.
God has enumerated everything in a record, supplying a comprehensive evidentiary basis for judgment.
Graves are overturned when the final reckoning begins, placing the hidden dead before judgment.
Every soul then knows what it sent ahead and left behind.
The one given a book in the right hand receives an easy account.
The Day exposes hidden secrets, making concealed human reality answerable.
Whoever does an atom's weight of good sees it.
Whoever does an atom's weight of evil sees it.
The graves are overturned, initiating disclosure before judgment.
What is within chests is brought out, exposing inward motives.
God is fully aware of people on that Day, completing the disclosure-and-accountability frame.
